newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint firms vs basket as dollar buying reduced.
newsitem.headline: Forint firms vs basket as dollar buying reduced.

text.p: Hungary's forint opened firmer against the currency basket on Friday as the recent rush of dollar-buying following pressure on the Polish zloty receded.
The forint, which usually trades at the central bank's resistance level, opened at around five pips inside the intervention band at 192.50/55 to the dollar and stood at 192.60/65 at 0745 GMT.
On Thursday the Hungarian unit ended 20 to 25 pips inside the band at 192.55/60 to noe dollar.

"There's still significant (dollar) buying interest from a couple of banks with large foreign customers," said Noemi Koppendorfer of ABN-AMRO Magyar Bank. "I expect buying to continue today but to die down in a few days."
The fall in the zloty was a result of the country's serious trade deficit combined with flood damage estimated at some $2 billion, traders said earlier.
As neither of these factors affects Hungary, the effect on the Budapest market was not expected to last.
The forint floats within the NBH's 4.5 percent wide intervention band, against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the ECU.
